title: The library that lends more than books
text: {{1}} decades, librarians have watched their job description quietly expand. Public libraries now lend {{2}} than books: tools, board games, sewing machines and, in the coldest months, simply {{3}} warm place to sit. {{4}} the shelves, they have become what sociologists call third places — neither home nor work, {{5}} the town square with a roof. Such is the demand {{6}} some newly built branches offer social workers, seed banks and recording studios alongside the novels. The card that once bought access to stories now opens a civic infrastructure, and librarians have become {{7}} engineers. Whatever the future of the printed page, the institution that guards it {{8}} decided to be useful first and quiet second.

gaps.explanation: 'More than' — the comparative of the expanded range.
